kai: ran a KV-frag stress smoketest on mistral / qwen hybrids with a couple of headcount tweaks. noticed a 18% p50 throughput drop on GQA path once paged-kv fragmentation hit ~62% :thinking:

marta: can you paste the test config? was this with num_key_value_heads reduced or increased?

kai: config below (simplified):
```
model: mixtral-mistral-hybrid
num_key_value_heads: 16 -> 12 (two variants)
kv_dim: 64
rope_scale: 1.04
kv_paging: enabled
slot_coalescer: off
batching: dynamic, max_batch_tokens=4096
```

kai: baseline (16 heads, slot_coalescer=on) p50=42.1k tok/s, when reducing to 12 heads with slot_coalescer off p50=34.5k tok/s. tail lat also spiked.

build-bot: deploy-log: kernel-picker pinned to avx2_fallback for the 12-head run, fallback count=3, kernel-switch events=127.

ashok: that kernel fallback is suspicious — did you force kernel affinity? sometimes when heads don't align with warp sizes we hit bad kernel selection and lots of small kernels which kills throughput.

kai: I didn't force it. kernel-picker selected avx2_fallback automatically after a couple of mispredicted head dims. we also saw high memcpy churn in the timeline.

zane: couple quick checks:
- confirm kv layout stride (interleaved vs packed)
- run with slot_coalescer on to see if fragmentation compacts
- try tiny rope_scale change back to 1.0 to see if RoPE interpolation triggers different kv indexing

marta: ran a mini repro with slot_coalescer toggled. results:
- slot_coalescer=on -> fragmentation ~12%, p50 back to 41k (+19% vs off)
- rope_scale 1.0 vs 1.04 -> negligible by itself but combined with 12 heads increased kernel-switches

kai: timeline snapshot (abridged):
```
00:00:00 batch start, 512 requests inflight
00:00:03 kv page fault thr: 46
00:00:03 kernel-switch event
00:00:09 memcpy 4.2ms spikes x 120
00:00:12 batch drain, p50 chunk=92ms
```

kai: hypothesis: when we reduce num_key_value_heads we change per-head size such that page packing becomes suboptimal for the current kv layout. this forces more fragmented page accesses, causing more memcpy and kernel fallbacks.

sre: sounds plausible. also if kernel heuristics use head count as an input they might pick kernels that expect different stride patterns. both effects multiply.

ashok: quick mitigation candidates:
- re-enable slot_coalescer as default when paged-kv enabled
- add kernel affinity probe at startup to pick best kernel per headcount/kv_dim combo (cheap microbench)
- try packing mode: pack-small-heads (attempt coalesced allocation)

kai: I ran the kernel-affinity probe idea locally: it added ~30ms startup but removed 80% of kernel-switches in the run. p50 improved 12% compared to naive run.

zane: longer-term we should teach kernel-picker to consider kv_fragmentation metric and prefer kernels with tolerant access patterns when fragmentation > threshold.

marta: agree. also worth adding a perf regression alert tied to these config flips (num_key_value_heads changes or rope_scale changes). caught this earlier by eyeballing timelines.

kai: next steps I'm taking:
- run a full matrix: heads={8,12,16,24}, kv_dim={32,64,128}, slot_coalescer={on,off}, rope_scale={1.0,1.04,1.08}
- add a microkernel probe to boot pipeline and record picks in telemetry
- small PR to default slot_coalescer=on for paged-kv until we have smarter packing

marta: if you add the telemetry tag, I'll hook a quick dashboard alert for fragmentation>45% + kernel-switches>30 in 60s window.

kai: thanks — will push results tomorrow. attaching raw perf csv to the thread in case anyone wants early access. :metal:

build-bot: artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-experiments/kv-frag/2425001111/smoke-results.csv

sre: nice repro. pls cc infra if you plan to flip slot_coalescer default — we should gate for Dedicated customer perf verification.

kai: will do. closing loop after full matrix.

marta: great — ping when matrix finished and we can schedule a short sync to roll mitigation plan. :white_check_mark:
